skill.name: css-colors
skill.description: Guidance for adding CSS colors through a Material UI theme instead of direct component color values.
skill.summary: Standardizes CSS color changes through theme palette and customColors usage.
skill.author: Crossbill-Highlights

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only skill file. Manual review found no executable code, network access, filesystem access, credential handling, or prompt injection attempt.

content.value_statement: Teams lose consistency when components use raw CSS color values. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use MUI theme colors.
actual_capabilities: Directs agents to prefer Material UI palette colors for CSS rules.
Points agents to frontend/src/theme/theme.ts as the theme source.
Discourages direct color codes inside component code.
Instructs agents to add needed new colors to the customColors section.
limitations: It is instruction-only and does not include executable tooling.
It does not define specific color token names or color values.
It does not validate contrast, accessibility, or brand compliance.
The referenced theme path may need adjustment in other projects.

use_cases.title: Replace raw component colors
use_cases.description: Convert component color values to existing theme palette references for cleaner frontend styling.

use_cases.title: Add a missing design token
use_cases.description: Place a required new color in customColors before using it across components.

use_cases.title: Review color consistency
use_cases.description: Check a change for direct color codes and request theme-based alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Use theme colors
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this component to replace direct CSS color values with MUI theme colors. Use existing palette values when possible.

prompt_templates.title: Add custom color
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this new design color. If no existing theme color fits, add a named value to customColors and use it in the component.

prompt_templates.title: Audit raw colors
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this feature for raw CSS color codes. Replace them with theme colors and list any new customColors entries needed.

prompt_templates.title: Plan color refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a safe color refactor across these files. Preserve behavior, prefer the MUI palette, and keep new tokens in customColors.

output_examples.input: A button component uses direct color values for background and hover states.
output_examples.output: The component now uses existing MUI theme palette values for both states. No new custom color was needed.

output_examples.input: A brand highlight color is missing from the current theme.
output_examples.output: A named customColors entry was added to the theme. Components reference that theme token instead of a direct color value.

output_examples.input: A feature branch contains several direct CSS color values.
output_examples.output: Direct values were replaced with theme references. Any unmatched colors were identified as customColors candidates for review.

best_practices: Check existing MUI palette values before adding any new color.
Keep component code tied to theme tokens instead of literal values.
Name customColors entries by purpose, not by visual appearance only.
anti_patterns: Do not scatter direct color codes across component files.
Do not add duplicate customColors entries for similar design needs.
Do not bypass the theme when a palette value already fits.

faq.question: Does this skill add colors automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for agents that edit or review frontend color changes.

faq.question: Which color source does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers Material UI palette values derived from frontend/src/theme/theme.ts.

faq.question: When should I add customColors?
faq.answer: Add customColors only when an existing palette value does not meet the design need.

faq.question: Does it allow direct hex values in components?
faq.answer: No. The guidance says component code should refer to theme colors instead.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it check color accessibility?
faq.answer: No. It does not validate contrast, accessibility rules, or brand approval.
